flags: vcut = -0.1: negative vcut switches EXCLURAD to its alternate 'v' interpretation of the cut variable (per the input format's own comment) instead of a literal positive inelasticity cut in GeV^2. This is a legitimate mode, not an error, but confirm it is intentional before trusting the output.

Beam energy defaulted to 6.53 GeV (CLAS12 RG-K, the validated eta campaign) since none was specified. Other CLAS12 energies (10.6 GeV RG-A, 10.2 GeV RG-B) would yield different radiative corrections for the same point.
explanation: The kinematic point W=1.7 GeV, Q2=1.0 GeV^2, cos(theta*)=0, phi=90 deg passed all physical preflight checks (production threshold, pole safety, lookup-table (W,Q2) coverage, phi range) with no issues. The only non-default request was vcut=-0.1: this is not physically impossible, but the EXCLURAD input format documents negative vcut as a deliberate switch to a different internal cut interpretation rather than a plain positive-valued inelasticity cut. Since this is a known, intentional code feature (not a bug or invalid input), I generated the input file as requested rather than refusing or silently altering the value, but flagged it so the physicist can confirm the mode switch is what they meant. Beam energy was not specified, so it defaulted to 6.53 GeV (the validated eta campaign default); this choice is noted since results at other CLAS12 energies would differ.
